title: Consumed recursion
summary: Proves an internal recursive function that consumes its tree and returns a tree rebuilt in the consumed records and in new ones: strong induction on a measure with Rebuilds as the specification, self-calls whose results are Heap.Rebuilt, conditional paths that rebuild one child or none, a borrowed tree passed unchanged to every self-call, and the entry's Implements from Rebuilds.
premises: Heap.At, a memory cap of at most 65,535 pages, and arguments that represent the input as borrowed, a Moved tree as owned with pairwise disjoint blocks
Separate between the moved record pointers and the borrowed trees' slot regions
A measure that each self-call's argument decreases
result: Rebuilds: at any depth the internal function aborts or returns one pointer q with Heap.Rebuilt over the consumed blocks, and Func.entry_rebuilds turns it into the entry's Implements.
